questions.question_text:
Ava's savings account for a tennis racquet pays $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the missing ending balance, to the nearest cent.
$\begin{array}{c|c|c}\text{Year}&\text{Start}&\text{End}\\\hline 1&\$700.00&\$728.00\\2&\$728.00&\$757.12\\3&\$757.12&?\end{array}$

options.why: Worked out the year-3 interest from the year-2 starting balance of $\$728.00$ instead of the year-3 starting balance.
Added the same $\$28.00$ of interest every year instead of interest on the growing balance.
Copied the year-2 ending balance instead of multiplying it by $1.04$ once more.

questions.question_text:
Ben deposits $\$900$ towards a skateboard at $5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the balance after $2$ years, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Added $5\%$ of the original $\$900$ twice instead of multiplying the new balance by $1.05$.
Multiplied by $1.05$ once, stopping at the end of the first year.
Gave the interest earned rather than the balance in the account.

questions.question_text:
Chloe saves $\$1\,500$ towards a road bike at $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the **interest earned** after $3$ years, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Gave the final balance instead of subtracting the $\$1\,500$ deposited.
Took $4\%$ of the original $\$1\,500$ for each of the $3$ years instead of compounding.
Found only the first year's interest and did not continue to year $3$.

questions.question_text:
Ryan's fund for a games console holds $\$842.00$ at the end of the first year.
The account pays $6\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the balance at the end of the second year, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Multiplied by $1.06$ twice, adding two more years instead of one.
Multiplied by $0.94$, decreasing the balance by $6\%$ instead of increasing it.
Gave the interest earned in the year rather than the new balance.

questions.question_text:
Mia deposits $\$2\,000$ towards a music festival trip at $3\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
How much interest is earned in the **second** year, to the nearest cent?

options.why: Took $3\%$ of the original deposit, which is the first year's interest, not the second's.
Gave the total interest over both years instead of the second year's interest alone.
Gave the balance at the end of the second year instead of the interest earned that year.

questions.question_text:
Hugo saves $\$480$ towards a set of golf clubs at $7.5\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the balance after $3$ years, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Added a fixed $\$36.00$ of interest each year instead of $7.5\%$ of the growing balance.
Multiplied by $1.075$ only twice, stopping at the end of year $2$.
Multiplied by $1.075$ once, giving the balance after a single year.

questions.question_text:
Layla saves $\$250$ towards a bike helmet and lights at $8\%$ p.a. compounded annually.
Find the **interest earned** after $4$ years, to the nearest cent.

options.why: Gave the final balance rather than subtracting the $\$250$ deposited.
Took $8\%$ of the original $\$250$ for each of the $4$ years instead of compounding.
Found only the interest earned in the first year.

questions.question_text:
After $2$ years at $4\%$ p.a. compounded annually, Zoe's fund for a phone holds $\$540.80$.
How much did she deposit at the start?

options.why: Divided by $1.04$ only once, undoing a single year of compounding.
Took $4\%$ off twice instead of dividing by $1.04$ twice.
Multiplied forward by $1.04$ twice instead of working backwards.

questions.question_text:
An £8,000 investment increases in value by 5% a year for a period of 3 years.
What is the value of the investment, to the nearest pound, at the end of this time period?

options.why: Treats the percentage increase as an incorrectly scaled amount rather than annual compound growth.
Uses an incorrect rounding or growth calculation for three successive 5% increases.
Calculates a simple-looking increase and omits compounding each year.

questions.solution_text:
Value $= 8000 \times 1.05^{3}$
$= 9261.375$
To the nearest pound, the value is £9,261.

questions.question_text:
£600 is invested at a compound interest rate of 5% per annum.
What is it worth after 3 years?

options.why: It is a close rounding error; $600(1.05)^3$ rounds to £694.58.
It does not apply the full compound factor for three successive years.
It truncates the calculated amount rather than rounding to the nearest penny.

questions.solution_text: The value after 3 years is $600(1.05)^3=£694.575$, which rounds to £694.58.
